findings.title: `over` sessions are named per product, not per family, so each family row lists every family's sessions
findings.description:
`_family_evidence` collects the named `over` sessions into a dict keyed by **product only** (`scripts/cutover_304_evidence.py`, `named.setdefault(product, []).extend(accounting.over_sessions(entry))`), and `over_failures` then reuses that one list for every family row of that product. The coverage document it is built from is the *statistics* read, whose `volume_checks` cover **every** volume family the entry wants — `tick_coverage_statistics._volume_checks` iterates `family_wants(entry)` filtered to `VOLUME_FAMILIES` = (`tick_tier`, `bar_1m`) (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_coverage_statistics.py:55-70`), and `volume_verdict_dict` emits each verdict's `family` (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_coverage.py:87-97`). `over_sessions` ignores that `family` field and does not filter.

Consequence: when ES `tbbo` has one `over` session and ES `ohlcv-1m` has three, both rows are emitted and both print all four session names — so the failure string under `ES tbbo` names bar sessions, and vice-versa. D6 item 4 asks for the `over` sessions named per family, and the counts in the same string (`row.cross_tier[VolumeClass.OVER.value]`) are correctly per-family, so the number and the names disagree. The fix is local: pass the family into `over_sessions` and filter on the verdict's `family` field (it is already in the document), or key `named` by `(product, family)`.

findings.title: `EXIT_USAGE` is defined but never referenced
findings.description: `EXIT_USAGE = 2` was added with the argparse work but no longer has a use: `main` returns the code argparse itself chose (`return int(exc.code or 0)`), which is exactly the convention `scripts/wal_segment_name.py` still spells with its own `EXIT_USAGE`. A named constant that no code path reads is dead, and it duplicates a value that argparse owns. Either drop it, or use it where the usage exit is produced so the value is defined once.

findings.title: `--estimate` prints no ceiling command when the estimate is `nothing_to_buy`, while the unset-ceiling hint points at that run
findings.description: `_estimate_only` only prints the command under `if outcome is Estimate.BUY`. In estimate mode `judge_estimate` returns `BUY` for any verdict except `nothing_to_buy` (`scripts/cutover_304_checks.py`, `if not check_ceilings: return Estimate.BUY`), so a `nothing_to_buy` estimate returns `NOTHING_TO_BUY` and no command is printed. But `check_env_text` runs unconditionally in the full cutover and raises `NO_CEILING_HINT` = "the PM sets the ceilings with the command the --estimate run prints" (`scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:39`). In that combination the operator is sent looking for a command the run never emitted. Printing the command whenever `summary["planned_usd"]` is parseable (harmless when nothing is to be bought) removes the dead end.

findings.title: `totals_delta` guards a family missing before the purchase but not one that vanishes after it
findings.description: The docstring states the one-directional rule ("a family absent before the purchase is a stop, not zero") and the code implements exactly that: `missing = sorted(set(after) - set(before))` raises, then the dict is built over `after` only. A family present in the baseline and absent in the after-read — the shape a reset, supersession or a dropped family would take — is silently omitted from the "before, after, delta" narration for D6 item 6 rather than reported. Checking the difference in both directions (or asserting the two key sets match) costs one line.

findings.title: Resubmit matching, ceiling derivation and gate ordering hold against the real producers
findings.description: Verified outside the diff: `ceiling_values`/`ceiling_command` use exact `Decimal` arithmetic with `ROUND_CEILING` on the step division and do not raise an exact multiple (89→90, 90→90, 6.3+4=10.3→15), and `:f` on a `steps * 5` product yields an integer literal because `to_integral_value` normalizes the exponent. `resubmit_origins` keys `(schema, range_start, range_end)` align with the estimate's `req["start"]`/`req["end"]` (`purchase_plan.py:290-293` → `TickRequest.start.isoformat()`) and with `_cell`'s date rendering, with the earliest `requested_at` winning on a shared range — a conservative choice that cannot report a match newer than it is. `run_gates` calls `check_gate_issue` then `check_dataset_edge` before `install_release` and before `record_start_and_baselines`, and `latest_want_end()` derives 2026-12-01T00:00Z from `_HISTORY_WANTS` rather than restating it in the script.

structured_findings.summary: `over` sessions are named per product, not per family, so each family row lists every family's sessions
`--estimate` prints no ceiling command when the estimate is `nothing_to_buy`, while the unset-ceiling hint points at that run
`totals_delta` guards a family missing before the purchase but not one that vanishes after it
